interest: Shows Japan seeking American bank credit in 1940 to buy China coast shipping, which U.S. consuls warned against.
overview: Section Three of Shanghai Telegram No. 883 (September 7, 1940, Butrick) warns that letting American banks finance Japanese coastal shipping in occupied China would set a damaging precedent.

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting on Japanese attempts to secure American bank financing and shipping tonnage in Shanghai and warning against creating a precedent for financing Japanese expansion in China.
subfiles.summary: Butrick reports Japanese efforts to finance China coast shipping through New York credits and Shanghai dollar purchases, warning against American bank accommodation.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 883 (Section Three) from Butrick (Shanghai) on Japanese Shipping and American Bank Financing in China
